Answer: C
Reason: Figure 1 shows bilateral alveolar opacities consistent with pulmonary edema from salt water aspiration, while Figure 2 demonstrates near-complete resolution of these opacities. Salt water aspiration causes non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema due to osmotic fluid shifts into the alveoli, which typically resolves with supportive care (oxygen and ventilation) as the lung epithelium heals, rather than requiring diuretics or antibiotics.
